prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1092; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change on a multi-lane roadway. Insured vehicle contacted the claimant's vehicle on the driver side rear quarter panel. Both drivers reported to be stopped at the scene and exchanged information. Police report requested, number pending. Initial liability appears to favor the claimant, pending statements from both parties.

Entry 2: Recorded recorded statement from the insured driver. States they checked mirrors and signaled but did not see the claimant's vehicle in the adjacent lane until contact. Insured acknowledges responsibility for the lane change but disputes that speed was a factor. Photos of both vehicles received and placed in file.

Entry 3: Contacted the claimant by phone. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and is handling the matter directly. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness beginning the following morning, consistent with whiplash. Claimant has scheduled an evaluation with their primary care provider and has been advised of the medical documentation needed for the bodily injury portion of the claim. Explained the general claims process and the claimant's right to seek independent legal advice at any time.

Entry 4: Received repair estimate for the claimant's vehicle from an appraiser. Damage includes rear door panel, quarter panel, and taillight assembly. Supplemental inspection requested due to possible hidden damage to the rear bumper bracket. Rental vehicle coverage confirmed for the claimant for the duration of repairs, subject to policy limits.

Entry 5: Medical records authorization sent to the claimant for signature. Follow-up call placed to check on symptoms and treatment progress. Claimant reports ongoing neck discomfort and is attending physical therapy sessions. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect current injury and property damage estimates. Next step is to await medical records and finalize liability determination.
